sections.h2: Can a Mesquite house sell quickly?
sections.html:
Often, yes. Your options are a cash buyer, a listing with an agent or a landlord, and the right one depends on how much repair the house needs and how soon you must close.

Mesquite is about 15 minutes east of downtown Dallas. Commuters, investors and landlords all shop here, a mix that suits a house with work you would rather not do.

Mesquite is a large Dallas suburb with more than 155,000 residents, covering almost 50 square miles. It calls itself the official Rodeo Capital of Texas. The town began as a Texas and Pacific Railway depot in 1873 and became a city on December 3, 1887.

Buyers like the roads. The city sits where Interstates 20, 30 and 635, State Highway 352 and U.S. Highway 80 meet, and both DFW International and Dallas Love Field are about 35 minutes away. Thousands of new homes are under construction, so expect new-build competition if you list on the open market.

sections.h2: Which sale routes fit a Mesquite house?
sections.html:
Owners here usually weigh four routes. Every one gives up price, speed or effort somewhere.

  • Agent listing. Likely the top price, with showings, repairs and lender hiccups landing on you.
  • Cash buyer. Fastest route, often with no repairs, with an offer that factors in what the buyer must spend.
  • Landlord or investor. Natural for houses with tenants; that buyer then deals with Mesquite's license rules.
  • Owner financing. You are paid over time, and Texas applies special contract rules while you hold title. See an attorney before agreeing.

Put cash offers next to a net estimate for listing. The difference is the price of speed.

Every rental in Mesquite must be registered, and a Single-Family Rental Property License is issued only after the home passes an inspection. A buyer who plans to rent the house will need to run this process.

Reviewers confirm that taxes are paid, no liens are outstanding, and a property manager or owner lives within 40 miles of Mesquite. A home that passes gets a green tag good for 90 days, during which the new tenant has to start water service. The license ends when the tenant changes or after three years with the same tenant, whichever comes first.

Review takes up to 48 business hours, and all utilities need to be running on inspection day. A separate short-term rental license costs $150 and expires each May 31.

An open permit can hold up a sale. Ask the city about any past work on the property. All permits must be finalized before a rental inspection, and the city publishes a document on permit requirements for unpermitted work.

Did you finish a garage, enclose a patio or swap out mechanical systems years back? Confirm the permit was closed. Cash buyers often accept the house as it stands, but a financed buyer's inspector may flag open permits. Phone the city's rental program office or the permit counter, and save receipts and final inspection records to hand the buyer.

sections.h2: Selling with a tenant in the house
sections.html:
Selling is possible, but whoever lives there holds legal rights until a formal process runs its course. The opening move is a written notice to vacate, three days minimum unless the lease sets another period. Hand it over, tape it inside the door, mail it, or email it if the lease allows.

If the tenant refuses to leave, the case moves to justice court. Four days must pass between service and trial, and the hearing itself is set 10 to 21 days from filing. County court appeals have to be made within five days of judgment, and six days after a final judgment the court can issue a writ of possession. A 30-day federal notice can also apply to some covered properties.

  • Many cash buyers take occupied houses and keep the lease.
  • A tenant change ends the city license, so a buyer who brings in new tenants must pass a fresh inspection.
  • Ask the justice court that serves Mesquite for filing details.

The sequence barely changes from one buyer type to the next. Once you know it, you can tell whether a promised closing date holds up.

  • Offer and contract: written terms are accepted and a title company opens the file.
  • Title search: liens, back taxes and recording defects get flagged.
  • Rental or permit review: a former rental or a house with remodeling needs its licenses and permits closed out.
  • Closing: everyone signs, the county clerk files the deed, and your net proceeds are released.

Buyers with a mortgage bring in an appraisal and underwriting. Cash buyers do without both, and that is mostly why their closings are faster. A few days before signing, ask your title contact for an estimated closing statement.

sections.h2: Property taxes when a Mesquite house sells
sections.html:
The lien attaches on January 1, which makes the owner on that date responsible for the year's bill. Statements arrive about October 1.

  • After January 31 penalty and interest begin to build.
  • Two payments are permitted, the first by November 30 and the second by June 30.
  • Owners aged 65 or older can split it into four.
  • A buyer who closes after January 1 can claim a homestead for the remaining months even if you never did.

Normally the title company divides the bill between you and the buyer and pays it from your funds. Ask to see the payoff and proration sheet before you sign.

Filing happens with the clerk of the county where the parcel is located. For reference, Dallas County received the first plat of the Mesquite townsite in 1873.

Before recording, a notary or similar officer has to acknowledge the signature. One 2023 clerk manual puts the charge at $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each extra page, with capped records fees added. Call the clerk for the current schedule.

sections.h2: What if I am behind on payments or inherited the house?
sections.html:
Time matters in both cases. A foreclosure ends at a public auction on a first Tuesday, once notice has been posted for 21 days. Paying what is overdue within 20 days of the default notice can stop it, and selling before the auction date protects your equity.

Inheriting a house starts a four-year clock to probate any will. Heirs showing who may sign might need a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit or a full administration, and a bare affidavit of heirship is sometimes refused by title companies.

Start with the deed, newest tax bill, payoff letter and any rental license or permit papers. Gather cash offers and set them beside a listing estimate. Get closing costs and timing from every buyer in writing.

faqs.q: How fast can a Mesquite house close on a cash offer?
faqs.a: Usually in a few weeks, because no lender underwriting or appraisal is involved. Liens and title work can add days, so put a target date in the contract.

faqs.q: Should I fix up the house first?
faqs.a: Not for a cash sale, where buyers usually accept the house as is. Repairs matter more if you list, since financed buyers bring appraisers who may require fixes.

faqs.q: Does the city regulate houses sold to landlords?
faqs.a: Every rental needs registration, an inspection and a local contact within 40 miles. The license lapses with a tenant change or after three years with the same tenant.
The title company prorates the year's bill and pays your portion from proceeds. Because the lien attaches January 1, review the split on the closing statement.

faqs.q: What happens to liens on the house?
faqs.a: Closing proceeds pay them off, as shown on a payoff statement from the title company. A rental review in Mesquite also wants taxes current and no open liens.
